rows.grounds: compound: maheśa+member, mala+member, māyā+member, ādi+member, vaśaga+head; sandhi noted in fused form

items.question: Why can the individual self not liberate itself while under higher powers?
premises: The individual self is under the control of the great lord, impurity, maya, and others
Being under such control limits autonomous action
items.inference: Therefore the individual self cannot achieve liberation by its own agency
items.plain_english: The individual self, being under the control of the great Lord, impurity, maya, and the rest, cannot by itself bring about its own liberation.

rows.grounds: compound: ātma+member, mocana+head; locative of purpose

items.question: What capacity does the individual self lack regarding its own liberation?
premises: Liberation requires an effective power to remove bondage
The individual self does not possess such power by itself
items.inference: Therefore the individual self has no power for its own liberation
items.plain_english: This self has no power for its own liberation, because it does not possess that power by itself.

items.question: Do individual selves or the bonds possess the power to bring liberation?
premises: Individual selves lack liberating power
Bonds are insentient and cannot remove themselves
items.inference: Therefore neither individual selves nor bonds have the power to effect liberation
items.plain_english: Neither individual selves have the power to bring about liberation, nor do the bonds have such power.

rows.grounds: at that time; fused form with following particle context
compound: nivartaka+member, tva+head; reason for agency
compound: na+member, adṛṣṭa+member, kalpanā+member, iti+head; fused form

items.question: Who must be the giver of liberation if selves and bonds cannot remove bondage?
premises: Neither selves nor bonds can effect liberation
Shiva alone is the remover of bondage
When a visible cause is established, an unseen cause need not be assumed
items.inference: Therefore Shiva alone is the giver of liberation to individual selves
items.plain_english: Since Shiva alone is the remover of bondage, he alone is the giver of liberation to souls; when this is seen, there is no need to assume an unseen cause.

rows.grounds: compound: jñatva+member, kartṛtva+head; dual abstract qualities

items.question: How do the bonds affect the manifestation of knowing and doing in the self?
premises: Knowing and doing are capacities of the self
Bonds condition how these capacities appear
items.inference: Therefore the bonds produce the manifestation of knowing and doing in many ways
items.plain_english: The bonds bring about the manifestation of knowing and doing in many different ways.

items.question: In what manner do the bonds shape the manifested knowing and doing?
premises: Bonds impose their own character on manifestation
The resulting manifestation inclines toward bondage
items.inference: Therefore the bonds make the manifestation colored by their own form and inclined to their functioning
items.plain_english: The bonds make that manifestation colored by their own form and inclined toward the functioning of bondage.

rows.grounds: compound: bhava+member, īrita+head; driven by worldly existence

items.question: Why do the bonds produce the manifestation of knowing and doing in bound existence?
premises: Bonds are unconscious
Bonds are impelled by worldly existence
items.inference: Therefore the bonds bring about the manifestation of knowing and doing without conscious intent
items.plain_english: Impelled by worldly existence and because of their unconsciousness, the bonds bring about the manifestation of those two.

items.question: How is the knowing-and-doing power characterized in relation to bonds and liberated selves?
premises: In ordinary states the power is manifested through bonds
In liberated selves the same power is identified as knowing and doing
items.inference: Therefore the power manifested by bonds is called the knowing-and-doing power of the liberated
items.plain_english: The power manifested by the bonds is called the knowing-and-doing power of the liberated.

items.question: What attachment arises when the self's power is manifested through bonds in the body?
premises: In the bound state the power is manifested by bonds
This manifestation occurs in the body and similar loci
items.inference: Therefore, like a bound self, it takes on attachment to identifying with the body as self
items.plain_english: Like that of a bound soul, when manifested by the bonds in the body and so on, it takes on attachment to grasping them as the self.

items.question: Does the arising or destruction of bonds alter the essential power of the self?
premises: Bonds may arise or be destroyed
The underlying power remains distinct from these changes
items.inference: Therefore that power is not divided or altered by the arising or destruction of bonds
items.plain_english: That power is not divided by bonds that arise or by bonds that are destroyed.

rows.grounds: compound: pāśa+member, pralaya+head; locative, fused form

items.question: Why does the liberated power remain unchanged even when the bonds dissolve?
premises: Bond dissolution removes limiting conditions
The liberated power abides in its own unchanged nature
It abides like the power of the Lord
items.inference: Therefore the liberated power remains unchanged even in the dissolution of bonds
items.plain_english: Even when the bonds dissolve, the liberated power abides in its own unchanged nature, just like the power of the Lord.

items.question: What is the scope of the liberated power compared to a limited power?
premises: The liberated power is not restricted by bonds
A limited scope would imply bondage-like restriction
items.inference: Therefore that power has all objects as its scope and is not of limited range
items.plain_english: That power has all things as its scope and is therefore not of limited range.

items.question: How does the liberated power differ from the power of a bound self in scope?
premises: The power of a bound self is sometimes limited to some object in some place
The liberated power is not similarly restricted
items.inference: Therefore the liberated power is not occasionally limited to some particular object like a bound self's power
items.plain_english: It is not, like the power of a bound soul, sometimes limited to some particular object in some particular place.

rows.grounds: compound: vyakti+member, antara+member, abhāva+head; ablative reason

items.question: Is the liberated power obstructed by the absence of another manifestation?
premises: Obstruction would require a conflicting manifestation
In the liberated state no such conflicting manifestation arises
items.inference: Therefore the liberated power is not obstructed by another manifestation merely due to its absence
items.plain_english: And that power is not obstructed by another manifestation merely because another manifestation is absent.

items.question: Why can the liberated power not be obstructed by any higher excellence?
premises: The liberated power is equal to Shiva
There is no further excellence beyond that equality
items.inference: Therefore the liberated power is not obstructed because no higher excellence exists beyond it
items.plain_english: The liberated power is not obstructed, because it is equal to Shiva and there is no further excellence beyond it.

items.question: Can the bonds manifest or overpower the liberated power after liberation?
premises: Bonds no longer function as manifestors in the liberated state
The liberated power is not subject to renewed subjugation
items.inference: Therefore the bonds neither manifest that power nor overpower it again
items.plain_english: The bonds do not manifest that power, nor is it ever overpowered by them again.

items.question: Under what condition does a manifested manifestation depend on a manifestor?
premises: A manifested manifestation requires a manifesting condition
Such dependence lasts only while the manifestor is present
items.inference: Therefore the manifestation of what is manifested lasts only as long as the manifestor is present
items.plain_english: The manifestation of what is manifested would last only so long as the manifestor is present.

items.question: What role does Shiva's power play in relation to the manifestor's proximity?
premises: Manifestation depends on a proximate manifesting cause
Shiva's power is the cause of manifestation
items.inference: Therefore Shiva's power constitutes the proximity that brings about manifestation
items.plain_english: The Shaiva power that causes manifestation is that very state of proximity.

items.question: Why can the bonds not be the cause for the distinct liberated power?
premises: The liberated power is distinct in nature
Bonds function only in conditioned manifestation
items.inference: Therefore the bonds are not the cause of that distinct liberated power
items.plain_english: Thus, for that distinct liberated power, the bonds are not the cause.

items.question: What is being identified as the cause of liberation in this context?
premises: The preceding verses negate other causes
A true cause of liberation must be identified
items.inference: Therefore the cause of liberation is being specified
uncertainties: This verse is a single token and may function as a heading or transition
items.plain_english: The cause of liberation.

items.question: Which practices are considered as possible means related to liberation or experience?
premises: Yoga and knowledge are proposed as means
Austerity and activities aimed at enjoyment are also considered
items.inference: Therefore yoga, knowledge, austerity, and activity for enjoyment are listed as candidate means
items.plain_english: Yoga, knowledge, austerity, and activity undertaken as a means to enjoyment.

items.question: Why is the mind insufficient as an ultimate liberating agent?
premises: The mind is insentient by nature
An insentient instrument cannot be the ultimate cause of liberation
items.inference: Therefore the mind, being insentient, cannot be the ultimate liberating cause
items.plain_english: The mind, because of its insentience.

items.question: Can even very intense practices sever the self from its bondage by themselves?
premises: Various means may be practiced intensely
Such means do not by themselves sever the self from bondage
items.inference: Therefore even very intense means do not cause the severing of the self from bondage
items.plain_english: Even very intense means do not by themselves cause the severing of one's own bondage.

rows.grounds: refers to a result or effect

items.question: Under what circumstance might a special transformation occur for someone through these means?
premises: Means by themselves do not guarantee liberation
A particular transformation may sometimes be connected with them
items.inference: Therefore, through connection with a special transformation, it may sometimes somehow occur for someone
uncertainties: The token 'ślo0 12' appears to be an editorial or citation marker within the verse text
items.plain_english: Through connection with a special transformation, that may sometimes somehow occur for someone — thus verse 12.
